summary: Handlers can now call `request.send_early_hints(...)` to send a 103 Early Hints response before the real one, and both `BaseHTTPMiddleware` and `GZipMiddleware` now pass those hints through instead of breaking on or dropping them.
overview: It's a new public method on `Request`, plus two pieces of plumbing so the method actually reaches the server. Class-based endpoints now give their `Request` a real `send` channel, and the two middlewares that sit between the app and the server learn about the `http.response.early_hint` ASGI message. Without the server's extension, the method does nothing.

effort.why: Small surface, but one subtle loop rewrite in BaseHTTPMiddleware.

checks.note: `Request.send_early_hints` sends `http.response.early_hint` with the links encoded as latin-1 bytes.
Signature is `send_early_hints(link, /, *additional_links)`: at least one link, no keywords.

checks.claim: Assert no Early Hints are sent without the extension
checks.note: The method checks `scope["extensions"]` and returns silently when the server doesn't advertise the extension.
`early_hint` joins `trailers` in the same pass-through branch of `IdentityResponder.send`.

checks.claim: (not stated) Class-based endpoints get a send channel
checks.note: `HTTPEndpoint.dispatch` now passes `send=self.send`. That also makes `request.send_push_promise` work in `HTTPEndpoint`s, where it used to raise.

architecture.summary: No new modules or dependencies. The change adds one public API and teaches the request path (endpoint → middleware → server) about one more ASGI message type that can arrive before `http.response.start`.

impact.title: `Request.send_early_hints(link, *additional_links)`
impact.detail: New public coroutine; a no-op unless the server advertises the `http.response.early_hint` extension.

impact.title: `HTTPEndpoint` requests can write to the response channel
impact.detail: The endpoint's `Request` now holds the real ASGI `send`, not the raising `empty_send`.

impact.title: `BaseHTTPMiddleware` forwards pre-response messages
impact.detail: It now reads messages in a loop until the response start, forwarding early hints to the server and recording debug info.

impact.title: `GZipMiddleware` passes early hints through
impact.detail: Before, an `early_hint` message matched no branch and was silently dropped.

flows.title: Through BaseHTTPMiddleware
flows.description: A handler sends one hint, then returns a response, behind a `BaseHTTPMiddleware`.

cases.label: Server supports early hints

before.text: treats it as the response start

cases.beforeOutcome: Nothing sent early hints before this PR. Had one arrived, the middleware read only the first message and would have taken it as the response start (unchecked).
cases.outcome: The 103 goes out first, then the normal response.

cases.label: Server without the extension
cases.outcome: Same as a request without hints: the call is a silent no-op.

decisions.title: No-op without the server extension
decisions.why: Handlers can call it unconditionally; only servers that advertise `http.response.early_hint` receive anything.

decisions.title: Positional-only links
decisions.why: At least one link is required by the signature itself. Each link is a full `Link` header value.

decisions.title: Forward hints inside the middleware's read loop
decisions.chose: a `while True` loop that forwards `early_hint` and keeps reading
decisions.over: buffering them until the response starts
decisions.why: Hints are useful only if they reach the client before the response, so they go to the server as soon as they arrive.

attention.title: BaseHTTPMiddleware now reads any number of pre-response messages
attention.why: The old code read one message, plus one more only if the first was a debug message. Now it loops past every `debug` and `early_hint` message until something else arrives.

attention.title: `send_push_promise` now works in `HTTPEndpoint`s
attention.why: It's a side effect of passing `send`: before, the endpoint's Request held `empty_send`, which raises when called.

steps.title: Add `send_early_hints` and give endpoint requests a send channel
steps.why: `Request.send_early_hints` encodes each link as latin-1 and sends one `http.response.early_hint` message, but only when the scope's extensions include it. `HTTPEndpoint.dispatch` now builds its Request with `send=self.send`, so the call can reach the server.
steps.effect: Function routes already had a send channel; class-based endpoints gain one.

notes: No extension, no message: the call returns silently
ASGI wants header values as bytes
Before: no send, so Request fell back to empty_send, which raises

steps.title: Let `BaseHTTPMiddleware` forward hints while it waits for the response
steps.why: `_CachedRequest` now takes `send` like `Request` does. The read of the app's first message becomes a loop: `debug` messages are recorded, `early_hint` messages are sent straight to the server, and the first other message ends the loop as before.
steps.effect: Hints sent from a handler behind any `BaseHTTPMiddleware` reach the client before the response.
steps.pseudocode:
loop:
  msg = next message from app
  debug      → remember info, keep reading
  early_hint → send to server now, keep reading
  otherwise  → this is the response start; stop

notes: So a handler's send_early_hints inside dispatch() has a channel too
Forwarded immediately instead of being mistaken for the response start
Same debug handling as before, now inside the loop

steps.title: Pass early hints through GZip untouched
steps.why: `IdentityResponder.send` groups `http.response.early_hint` with `http.response.trailers` in the branch that forwards the message as-is.
steps.effect: Before, the message matched no branch and was dropped.

steps.title: Test the method, the endpoint, and both middlewares
steps.why: Each test sends a hint and asserts the message order the server sees: `early_hint` first, then `http.response.start`, then the body. Two request tests cover the no-extension and no-send-channel cases.
steps.effect: Covers every path in the diagram; nothing runs against a real server.

notes: Without the extension nothing is sent
Two hints (endpoint + middleware) arrive before the start

stopped.why: They used to match no branch in `IdentityResponder.send`.

stopped.what: Requests in `HTTPEndpoint` no longer hold the raising `empty_send`
